origin_line: Founded by Cristóbal Balenciaga; the Paris house opened in 1937.

lead_line: Sharply tailored, dark-romantic fashion from the London house founded by Lee Alexander McQueen.
origin_line: Founded in London in 1992 by Lee Alexander McQueen, who had trained on Savile Row.

lead_line: Deconstructed, conceptual clothing — exposed seams, rebuilt garments — with the artisanal line made by hand in the atelier.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 1988 by Martin Margiela.

lead_line: Dark, draped clothing in leather, cashmere and jersey, made in the company's own factory in Italy.
origin_line: Founded in Los Angeles in 1994 by Rick Owens; the company now owns its Italian factory.

lead_line: Loose, draped clothing, mostly black, in wool gabardine and other cloth.
origin_line: Founded in Tokyo by Yohji Yamamoto; first Paris show in 1981.

lead_line: Experimental clothing that questions how garments are built and worn; sold through Dover Street Market and its own stores.
origin_line: Founded in Tokyo in 1969 by Rei Kawakubo.

lead_line: Reworked workwear and denim — patchwork, hybrid pieces, collaborations with Levi's, Carhartt and The North Face — from a Comme des Garçons designer.
origin_line: Junya Watanabe has had his own line within Comme des Garçons since 1992.

lead_line: Hybrid clothing that splices two garments into one — a shirt and a knit, a bomber and a coat.
origin_line: Founded in 1999 by Chitose Abe, formerly of Comme des Garçons.

lead_line: Printed silk shirts and sport-influenced clothing in bright colors.
origin_line: Founded in 2018 by Charaf Tajer.

lead_line: Sculptural, sun-drenched clothing in a Provençal palette; the men's line is the smaller part.
origin_line: Founded in 2009 by Simon Porte Jacquemus at 19; named for his mother.

lead_line: Clothing, leather goods and Re-Nylon, from a Milan house known for deliberately odd design choices.
origin_line: Founded in Milan in 1913 by Mario Prada as a leather-goods shop; led by Miuccia Prada since 1978.

lead_line: Leather goods and craft-led fashion, with menswear under Jonathan Anderson's direction until 2025.
origin_line: Founded in Madrid in 1846 as a leather workshop.

lead_line: Jonathan Anderson's own label — playful, odd British design, from a pigeon-shaped clutch to shrunken knitwear.
origin_line: Founded in London in 2008 by Jonathan Anderson.

lead_line: The Paris house's menswear — tailoring, sneakers, logo pieces — under a succession of creative directors.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 1947 by Christian Dior.

lead_line: Distressed denim, leather and casual clothing that began with rock musicians and now shows in Paris.
origin_line: Founded in Los Angeles in 2014 by Mike Amiri.

lead_line: American sportswear references — racing graphics, track pants — at runway prices.
origin_line: Founded in Los Angeles in 2015 by Rhuigi Villaseñor.

lead_line: Track suits and skate-influenced clothing made in Italy, sold at luxury prices.
origin_line: Founded in 2015 by Francesco Ragazzi, out of his 2014 photo book of Venice Beach skaters.

lead_line: Hand-distressed Italian sneakers, with a clothing line built out from them.
origin_line: Founded near Venice in 2000 by Francesca Rinaldo and Alessandro Gallo.

lead_line: Loose, long-proportioned casual clothing and tailoring; made with Zegna under a partnership.
origin_line: Founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by Jerry Lorenzo.

lead_line: One-of-a-kind garments cut from antique quilts, tablecloths and textiles.
origin_line: Founded in New York in 2016 by Emily Adams Bode.

lead_line: One-of-a-kind garments rebuilt from vintage military cloth, tents and denim in a Los Angeles studio.
origin_line: Founded in 2011 by Greg Lauren, a painter and Ralph Lauren's nephew.

lead_line: Clothing and footwear made with traditional techniques — natural dyes, hand-loomed cloth — at high prices.
origin_line: Founded in Tokyo in 2001 by Hiroki Nakamura, formerly a designer at Burton.

lead_line: Sharp, glamorous tailoring and eveningwear.
origin_line: Founded in 2006 by Tom Ford after leaving Gucci.

lead_line: Ralph Lauren's top line — tailoring, cashmere and shoes made in Italy.
origin_line: Launched in 1994.

lead_line: Suits, tailoring and knitwear from a company that owns its wool mill in Biella and traces its fiber.
origin_line: Founded in Trivero, Italy, in 1910 by Ermenegildo Zegna as a wool mill.

lead_line: Leather goods in woven intrecciato leather and clothing to match, with no visible logo.
origin_line: Founded in Vicenza in 1966.

lead_line: Shoes in patinated leather, from a Paris bootmaker, with a clothing line added.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 1895 by Alessandro Berluti.

lead_line: Made-to-measure and ready-made shirts and ties from the Place Vendôme shop.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 1838 by Christofle Charvet, the first shop devoted to shirts.

lead_line: Strong-shouldered tailoring in a 1970s style, from Paris.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 2011 by Nicolas Gabard.

lead_line: Roman tailoring, made to measure and ready to wear, at the top of the market.
origin_line: Founded in Rome in 1945 by Nazareno Fonticoli and Gaetano Savini.

lead_line: Neapolitan tailoring in bold colors and lightweight cloths.
origin_line: Founded in Naples by the Isaia family, in the fabric trade from the 1920s and making tailoring by 1957.

lead_line: Plain, expensive clothing in the finest fabrics, with nothing on it.
origin_line: Founded in 2006 by Ashley and Mary-Kate Olsen, starting with a T-shirt.

lead_line: Loose, muted clothing with a utilitarian feel, from Paris.
origin_line: Founded in Paris by Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran.

lead_line: Minimalist tailoring and clothing in a precise cut, from the house that defined the style.
origin_line: Founded in Hamburg in 1968 by Jil Sander.

lead_line: Scandinavian fashion — denim, knitwear, outerwear, the Canada scarf — from Stockholm's largest fashion company.
origin_line: Founded in Stockholm in 1996 by Jonny Johansson and partners; the clothing line began in 1997 with 100 pairs of jeans given to friends.

lead_line: Printed, patterned clothing from the Antwerp designer, independent for most of its history.
origin_line: Founded in Antwerp in 1986 by Dries Van Noten, one of the Antwerp Six.

lead_line: Tailoring and sportswear drawing on Black Atlantic style history; the Adidas collaboration revived the Samba.
origin_line: Founded in London in 2014 by Grace Wales Bonner.

lead_line: Clothing dyed by weather — garments left outdoors for months so sun, wind and rain fade them — on reconstructed vintage cloth.
origin_line: Founded in Seoul around 2020 by Jiyong Kim, who trained at Bunka and Central Saint Martins and worked at Lemaire and Louis Vuitton.

lead_line: Cashmere knitwear and soft tailoring in muted colors, made in Umbria.
origin_line: Founded in 1978 by Brunello Cucinelli, who dyed cashmere in bright colors when it was sold only in neutrals; based in Solomeo.

lead_line: Knitwear — four-ply cashmere, Giza cotton piqué polos — from a family company in Monza.
origin_line: Founded in Monza in 1934 by the Fedeli family.

lead_line: Hand-loomed, hand-dyed cashmere from Los Angeles, including tie-dye.
origin_line: Founded in Los Angeles in 2007 by Greg Chait, starting with a cashmere blanket.

lead_line: Leather goods, silk and clothing made in the company's own workshops, with no licensees.
origin_line: Founded in Paris in 1837 by Thierry Hermès as a harness maker.

lead_line: Cashmere, vicuña and fine-wool clothing from a company that controls its raw materials; owned by LVMH.
origin_line: The Loro Piana family have traded wool in Piedmont since the early 1800s; the company dates from 1924.

lead_line: Neapolitan tailoring from the house that developed the soft Neapolitan cut.
origin_line: Founded in Naples in 1932 by Gennaro Rubinacci as London House.

lead_line: Hand-made Neapolitan tailoring from a company with its own tailoring school and wool mill.
origin_line: Founded in Arzano, near Naples, in 1968 by Ciro Paone.

lead_line: Neapolitan tailoring from the family credited with the unpadded Neapolitan shoulder.
origin_line: Vincenzo Attolini developed the soft shoulder at Rubinacci in the 1930s; the house carries his son's name.

lead_line: Leather, cashmere and silk clothing at the very top of the market, from Lyon.
origin_line: Founded in Lyon in 1965.

lead_line: Silk ties, shirts and clothing in an opulent Florentine style.
origin_line: Founded in Florence in 1972 by Stefano Ricci.

lead_line: Cashmere and wool knitwear and cloth from a working Scottish mill.
origin_line: Founded in Elgin, Scotland, in 1797.
